header.title: Open Energy Studio
header.heroAlt: Open Energy Studio: results for a fictitious terraced house with energy label A+, BENG 1, 2 and 3, TOjuli and the monthly energy use
header.label: Energy performance
header.tagline: BENG, energy label and TOjuli following NTA 8800, step by step and traceable down to the formula
header.desc: Answer the questions on project, building and installations step by step, and watch the label class and the BENG indicators follow every change. For new and existing buildings, dwellings and non-residential buildings, with report and tailored advice.

meta.description: Free, open-source energy performance software following NTA 8800: BENG 1, 2 and 3, energy label and TOjuli for dwellings and non-residential buildings, with calculation trace, report and tailored advice. Test version without BRL 9501 attestation. For Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser.
meta.title: Open Energy Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

envelope.alt: Building step: table of walls, roofs, floor and windows by orientation, with slope, area and construction, and the provisional result on the right
envelope.title: The building envelope, surface by surface
envelope.desc: Record walls, roofs, floors and windows with orientation, slope, area and construction. Envelope checks and the transmission loss per element type show right away where the heat escapes.

installations.alt: Installations step: an HR107 boiler with the questions on generation, distribution, emission, control and auxiliary energy, and a source for each input
installations.title: Installations without missing a thing
installations.desc: Heating, domestic hot water, ventilation, cooling and solar panels, each in fixed steps from generation to auxiliary energy. For every input you note where it comes from, such as the rating plate or the drawing.

trace.alt: Calculation trace: the monthly transmission with the formula, the values used, the result and the NTA 8800 formula number
trace.title: Every result can be checked
trace.desc: The calculation trace shows, step by step, the formula, the values used, the result and the NTA 8800 formula number. Search for a surface or quantity, expand what you want to see and export the trace.

report.alt: Report and file: choice between summary, standard and detailed, with the calculations to tick and a preview of the report
report.title: A report at the level you need
report.desc: Choose summary, standard or detailed, and tick which calculations go in down to monthly level. Download it as a PDF, and also produce an input file and the BRL 9500 checklist.

tools.alt: U-value calculator: a cavity wall with brick, cavity, mineral wool and plasterboard, the cross-section to scale and the Rc and U value
tools.title: U value, thermal bridge and heat pump at hand
tools.desc: Calculate the Rc and U value of a build-up layer by layer, with a cross-section to scale. There is also a thermal bridge calculator and an aid for sizing a heat pump.

notice.text: Test version without BRL 9501 attestation: results are indicative. Testers wanted, especially energy and EPA advisors.

features.label: Features
features.heading: From the first question to the report, in one workflow
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

steps.title: Work in steps
steps.desc: Project, building, installations and check: each step asks the questions that matter. Skipping is fine; the engine reports what is really missing.

live.title: Results update as you go
live.desc: Label class, BENG 1, 2 and 3 and TOjuli are visible at every step and recalculate with every change.

zones.title: Zones and envelope
zones.desc: Calculation zones, surfaces and windows, constructions, thermal bridges, airtightness and unheated spaces.

systems.title: All installations
systems.desc: Heating, hot water, ventilation, cooling and solar power, down to shower heat recovery.

evidence.title: A source for every input
evidence.desc: Link photos, drawings or rating plates to the input, so you know later where a value came from.

uvalue.title: U-value calculator
uvalue.desc: Rc and U of a wall, roof or floor, layer by layer, with a cross-section to scale.

bridge.title: Thermal bridge calculator
bridge.desc: Work out the effect of a thermal bridge before you enter it.

heatpump.title: Heat pump sizing
heatpump.desc: A calculation aid for the capacity a heat pump needs.

overview.title: BENG check at a glance
overview.desc: For each indicator the value, the requirement and how far above or below it you are, with points of attention and the article from the Bbl.

monthly.title: Monthly values and charts
monthly.desc: Energy use per service, per carrier and per month, and the heating and cooling demand, also as a table.

trace.title: Calculation trace
trace.desc: Every step with formula, values, result and formula number, searchable and exportable.

provenance.title: Where the result comes from
provenance.desc: Engine version, norm edition and a fingerprint of the input, plus the interpretations the engine chose.

editions.title: Older norm editions
editions.desc: Also calculate with the 2024, 2023, 2022 and 2020+A1 editions, clearly marked as not registrable.

report.title: Report at three levels
report.desc: Summary, standard or detailed, as a PDF or printed, with a separate report for tailored advice.

dossier.title: File in one ZIP
dossier.desc: Input, report and evidence together, with a manifest and a checksum per file.

eponline.title: Overview in EP-Online layout
eponline.desc: The data as the EP-Online export expects it, with the field limits. Registering requires an attestation first.

survey.title: Survey of existing buildings
survey.desc: Survey of existing dwellings and non-residential buildings following ISSO 82.1 and 75.1; the answers become project input.

advice.title: Tailored advice
advice.desc: Calculate measures and packages on actual use: savings, CO₂, costs, payback time and net present value.

relabel.title: Relabelling
relabel.desc: Compare the original and the improved project, so you see what the improvement achieves.

exchange.title: Uniec 3 and VABI
exchange.desc: Import projects from Uniec 3 and VABI Elements, with a list of all assumptions. Export to VABI.

ifc.title: 3D model and IFC
ifc.desc: View zones, surfaces, windows and solar panels in 3D and export the model as IFC.

api.title: API and MCP
api.desc: All 46 calculation operations through a local HTTP API or as MCP tools for an AI assistant.

local.title: Your projects stay with you
local.desc: The web version calculates in the browser and keeps projects there; no project data goes to a server.

manual.title: Manual in the app
manual.desc: A Dutch-language manual per topic, with a button on every page to the right chapter.

download.title: Download v2026.44.0
download.lead: Free, no account needed. For Windows, macOS and Linux.
download.browserNote: Rather not install anything? The app also runs in the browser.
download.label: Download
download.mobileNote: Open Energy Studio is made for a large screen. Open it on your computer, or try it here in the browser.

tojuli.title: Traceable TOjuli
tojuli.desc: All terms of the formula per orientation, and the fixed values per zone.

update.title: New version notice
update.desc: The desktop app reports a newer release with a button to the download; can be turned off in the settings.

uniecgeo.title: Geometry to Uniec
uniecgeo.desc: Draft: a ground-level dwelling to the Uniec geometry import (Excel). Not yet tested in Uniec itself.

uniecimport.title: Uniec import tells you more
uniecimport.desc: Reports a second building in the file and lists every assumption, with type and field.

confirm.title: Check imports first
confirm.desc: An import from Uniec or VABI only counts for registration once the advisor confirms it has been checked.

recovery.title: Recovery copy
recovery.desc: If the browser refuses autosave, the app retries and reports it in the status bar.

whatsnew.label: New in v2026.44
whatsnew.title: TOjuli traceable, Uniec export in draft
whatsnew.desc: Engine 0.5.0 makes TOjuli traceable down to the formula, the Uniec import tells you more, and the desktop app now reports when a new version is out.

files.a: Your own projects (.oes.json) and exchange files from Uniec 3 (.uniec3) and VABI Elements (.epa or .xml). For every import the app keeps the file name, a checksum and a list of assumptions and issues.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. The web version runs straight in the browser and calculates there too: your project data does not go to a server. If you want to keep projects as files on your own disk, install the desktop app.

price.q: What does Open Energy Studio cost?
price.a: Nothing. The app is free and open source under the LGPL-3.0, with no account or subscription. The NEN and ISSO norm texts are not included; you need your own copies.

save.q: In which format is my work saved?
save.a: In an open JSON file (.oes.json). In the browser, projects are kept in that browser; the desktop app saves them as files. The project file can be exported as a ZIP.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows 10 and 11, macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Linux (.deb, .rpm and AppImage), and any modern browser. The Windows installer is signed; the macOS version is not yet, so open it the first time with right-click and Open.

practice.a: Yes. It calculates following NTA 8800:2025+C1:2026 with the BENG requirements from the Bbl, and follows ISSO 82.1, 75.1, 82.2 and 75.2 and BRL 9500 for surveys and advice. Exchange with Uniec 3 and VABI is built in.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: There is an MCP server and a local HTTP API with the same 46 operations as the engine. An assistant can use them to calculate a project or consult the manual. For now you build both yourself from the source code.

label.q: Can I register an official energy label with it?
label.a: Not yet. Open Energy Studio does not (yet) hold a BRL 9501 attestation. Results are indicative and cannot be used for an official energy label, a BENG check for a permit or registration in EP-Online. The app and the reports say so too.

verify.q: How do I know the result is right?
verify.a: Every result carries the engine version and a fingerprint of the input, and the calculation trace shows every formula. The engine is tested against public calculation reports and the RVO example dwellings; the differences are explained item by item in the documentation.

testers.a: Please do, especially if you are an energy or EPA advisor. Calculate a project you know and report differences or bugs through an issue on GitHub.

rust.title: Rust calculation engine
rust.desc: A deterministic NTA 8800 core without I/O; every result carries the engine version and a SHA-256 of the input.

wasm.title: WebAssembly
wasm.desc: The same core runs in the browser, so the web version calculates without a server.

tauri.title: Tauri 2
tauri.desc: A native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, with a signed Windows installer.

react.title: React and TypeScript
react.desc: One interface for browser and desktop, with forms tested against the engine.

api.title: HTTP API and MCP
api.desc: 46 operations from one registry, as an OpenAPI 3.1 API and as MCP tools over stdio.

gate.title: Verification gate
gate.desc: Every calculation change passes unit tests, independent recalculations from the norm text, fuzz tests and reference suites.
